header: Rate of crime per 1,000,000 of population

notes: The volume of crime which had shown an upward trend in the years 1961/1962 and dropped slightly during the year 1963 has again shown rise in the year under review.

The increase in crime is attributed generally to adverse economic conditions, rising cost of living, increase in the population, corresponding growth and shift in it, rapid industrialisation, insufficient attention to the prevention of crime due to pre-occupation of the police with law and order problems, factionalism in villages, and better reporting and registration of cases. The increase is also partly due to the fact that a number of Union Territories have now been brought under the purview of this report.
